## Year 10 recap: expanding one bracket {#single-bracket}

We are learning to expand brackets using FOIL and two identities.

I can recognise a perfect square or a difference of two squares and choose a method to expand it.

Recall: multiply the term outside the bracket by each term inside. Keep each sign with its term. Try the example on paper before selecting **Next**.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$3x(2x-5)$

::: {.fragment}

[Multiply both terms by $3x$.]{.annotation}

$=(3x)(2x)+(3x)(-5)$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Multiply the coefficients and the variables.]{.annotation}

$=6x^2-15x$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$-3x(2x-5)$

Predict the sign of each product, then expand on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$=(-3x)(2x)+(-3x)(-5)$

$=-6x^2+15x$

The second product is positive because both factors are negative.

:::
